code: while (lexer->start < lexer->end) { c = *lexer->start++; if (njs_tokens[c] != NJS_TOKEN_SPACE) break; }
note: The attacker-controlled script bytes are consumed from the heap input buffer. For input '1+' the first token consumes '1', and the next call consumes the final '+' so that lexer->start == lexer->end.
The final byte '+' is classified as NJS_TOKEN_ADDITION by the njs_tokens table, selecting the multi-character operator branch.

code: case NJS_TOKEN_ADDITION: njs_lexer_multi(lexer, token, njs_addition_token, njs_nitems(njs_addition_token)); break;
note: The switch dispatches to njs_lexer_multi() to check whether the operator is actually a longer multi-character token (e.g. '++' or '+='). lexer->start points exactly at the end of the buffer.

Root cause: njs_lexer_multi() dereferences lexer->start[0] with no 'lexer->start < lexer->end' guard. When the operator byte is the final byte of the script, lexer->start == lexer->end and the dereference targets the byte past the end of the heap buffer.
Sink: the load of lexer->start[0] with lexer->start == lexer->end reads one byte beyond the heap-allocated input buffer, producing the reported heap-buffer-overflow.
